site.name: Apollo 17 lunar module (Taurus-Littrow valley)
site.coordinate_frame: Lunar mean Earth/polar axis (ME) system, as stated by the source; planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude. The source names no ephemeris realization; DE421 (as the DEM and Horizons MOON_ME) is assumed.
site.coordinate_source_title: LROC: Spacecraft Related Coordinates - 2016 Update (M. Robinson, 25 November 2016): Apollo 17 LM 20.1911, 30.7723, elevation -2626 m (GLD100), uncertainty 3.5 m; see Wagner et al. 2017, Icarus 283, 92-103
site.coordinate_source_product: LROC featured image 938 table (means of multiple NAC images); Wagner et al. (2017) doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.05.011
site.point_description: the Apollo 17 lunar module descent stage, landed 1972-12-11, located in LROC NAC images
site.coordinate_accuracy_note: table uncertainty 3.5 m (column not defined on the page); the page gives about +/-15 m for latitude/longitude in general
site.surface_elevation_reference: Height above the 1737.4 km sphere, SLDEM2015 512 px/deg tile sldem2015_512_00n_30n_000_045_float (LOLA + SELENE TC, Barker et al. 2016), bilinear at the published point interpreted in ME. Rounded to 0.1 m. LROC's table gives -2626 m from GLD100 (a different shape model; 2.0 m higher). See data/terrain/apollo17-lm_site_elevation_report.json.
site.horizons_altitude_reference: Height above the Horizons reference body for the Moon: a 1737.4 km sphere (response header 'Center radii'), the same reference as SLDEM2015 heights.
site.altitude_conversion_note: horizons_site_altitude_km = (surface_elevation_m + observer_height_above_surface_m) / 1000 = (-2628.0 m + 1 m) / 1000 = -2.627 km (negative: the site lies below the 1737.4 km sphere). Both heights are relative to the 1737.4 km sphere, so no datum conversion is needed. Rounding: the bilinear SLDEM2015 surface is -2627.9921 m; rounded to 0.1 m before forming the altitude, the submitted point is 0.9921 m above the interpolated surface (nominal 1 m). The generic terrain horizon and rendering use this same configured observer; no observer substitution is made.
